devices.role: recording rig for the committed client-performance baseline (run-2026-09-03, results-2026-09-04, and the 2026-09-05 target-4 argon re-record)
devices.note: desktop Chromium on the actual recording machine, unthrottled; not a physical mobile device. Physical-device rows replace or extend this scope at qualification time.

note: Real measured p95 budgets, recorded on the lab rig (MacBook-Pro.local, 18 x Apple M5 Pro, Chromium 151.0.7922.34; the unthrottled mainstream-desktop tier IS the actual recording machine) at the real challenge configurations: Argon2id at the round-5 retuned adaptive-risk ladder (m=16384 KiB, t=3, p=1, target 4; the 8-bit rung of the earlier rows measured ~16 s p95, above the absolute 5000 ms UX ceiling that made the retune necessary), the rsw time-lock rungs at T=75,000 / 150,000 / 300,000 squarings (the default rung, the midpoint and the protocol ceiling of 10,000..=300,000), SHA-256 at 16/18/20 bits, and the ExecutionChallengeV1 cells (the files-tier execvm/execsha18/execargon/execchain and the inline-tier execvminline/execsha18inline). Every row is ceil(1.2 x merged p95) of the measurements in tools/client-perf/results/baseline.json: the p95 is computed over the concatenated repetitions of the cell's asset modes (the harness percentile semantics), and the fixed 20% margin is the documented allowance for the CDP-emulation noise this lab itself measures, not a placeholder factor. Evidence runs: results/run-2026-09-03.json (desktop real-ladder run, 12 SHA / 6 Argon reps per mode), tools/client-perf/results/results-2026-09-04.json (focused run, 50 reps, the rsw rungs and the inline execution cells), tools/client-perf/results/results-2026-09-05.json (the round-5 target-4 re-record of the argon family, argon2id/execargon/execchain, 12 Argon reps per mode: argon2id p95 621/850 ms, execargon p95 1179/877 ms, execchain p95 709/1111 ms cold/warm), and tools/client-perf/results/results-2026-09-05-exec-v5.json (the live-grammar execution re-record, audit finding 1: every armed cell ran with ?exec_cap=5, the protocol/execution-v1.json manifest maximum — the earlier execution rows measured the fixture's historical v3 default — 20 SHA-profile / 12 Argon reps per mode, every rep decoding executionVersion 5; execvm p95 16/22 ms, execsha18 p95 1446/1471 ms, execargon p95 912/615 ms, execchain p95 556/860 ms, execvminline p95 19/19 ms, execsha18inline p95 320/363 ms cold/warm). absoluteP95Ceilings declares the absolute interactive UX ceiling of every certified tier (5000 ms solve and page-to-verified p95 on mainstream-desktop): a budget row above the ceiling is a hard rejection even when measurements are below it. The interactive/non-interactive classification derives from the harness difficulty profiles in tools/client-perf/client-perf.mjs (audit finding 4): execchain carries interactive: false — it is budgeted and measured like every cell but is never counted as an ordinary interactive release cell (it models the composed chained-escalation flow, a SHA request escalated to the memory-hard rung, whose p95 is not the experience of an interactive rung a user is sent to directly) — and every other difficulty is interactive and ceiling-subject. The budgets file itself declares no classification and cannot change one. The qualified tier scope is mainstream-desktop only: it is the tier that represents the actual lab hardware. The five emulation tiers (low-android, mid-android, flagship-android, older-iphone, current-iphone) and low-desktop carry no budget rows because no real-ladder qualification evidence exists for them; emulation tiers are calibration signals, never release boundaries. The release-gate procedure (physical-device qualification replacing this file tier by tier) is documented in tools/client-perf/README.md. qualification.release_tiers names the release-certification ladder (mainstream-desktop today, the only tier with real-harness evidence); extending the ladder means adding that tier's p95 budget rows, its absoluteP95Ceilings entry and its physical-device evidence, never an invented tier name.
